events.title: Samuel Pepys Ends His Famous Diary
events.description: Worried that failing eyesight was making the work too hard, Samuel Pepys wrote his last entry in the diary he had kept since 1660. The diary covers the Great Plague, the Great Fire of London and the early years of the Restoration.
events.significance: Pepys's diary is one of the best firsthand records of daily life in 17th-century England. Historians still use it today.

events.title: The Johnstown Flood
events.description: After days of heavy rain, the South Fork Dam in western Pennsylvania failed. A wall of water swept through Johnstown and the surrounding valley, killing more than 2,200 people.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest disasters in American history. It prompted early large-scale disaster relief by the American Red Cross and shaped US legal ideas about liability.

events.title: Mongols Triumph at the Kalka River
events.description: A Mongol army led by the generals Subutai and Jebe defeated a combined force of Kievan Rus' princes and Cuman allies near the Kalka River, in what is now Ukraine.
events.significance: The victory showed how formidable the Mongol military was in Eastern Europe. It foreshadowed the full Mongol invasion of the Rus' lands about fifteen years later.

events.title: The Treaty of Vereeniging Ends the Boer War
events.description: Representatives of the Boer republics signed the Treaty of Vereeniging, ending the Second Boer War. The Transvaal and the Orange Free State accepted British sovereignty.
events.significance: The treaty brought British control over all of South Africa. It paved the way for the Union of South Africa, which was created in 1910.
